facets.answer: Cloud infrastructure investment supports NVIDIA’s outlook by creating substantial potential demand for data-center GPUs and networking. Five hyperscalers’ 2026 AI-infrastructure spending is forecast at about $800 billion, and Alphabet and Amazon have raised their 2026 capex guidance. This is planned or forecast spending, not completed investment, and it does not show how much will go to NVIDIA.

Conversion has already occurred at scale: NVIDIA reported FY2026 revenue of $215.9 billion, including $193.7 billion from Data Center. FY2027 Q1 Data Center revenue was $75.2 billion, up 92% year over year, with NVIDIA citing the Blackwell 300 ramp and networking demand. A signed $240 million IBM–Together AI agreement to build a cluster using NVIDIA systems is concrete customer activity. However, the card does not reconcile hyperscaler capex to NVIDIA orders, shipments, or future recognized revenue; planned deployments and production readiness do not establish revenue amount or timing. NVIDIA’s $91.0 billion FY2027 Q2 revenue figure is guidance, not a realized result.

Conversion depends on customers’ ability to secure data-center capacity, energy, and capital; NVIDIA says shortages could affect future revenue. Revenue concentration is material: three direct customers represented 21%, 17%, and 16% of FY2027 Q1 total revenue, primarily in Compute & Networking. NVIDIA also says it was effectively foreclosed from China’s data-center compute market. The announced financing platform of more than $500 billion is neither NVIDIA revenue nor a single committed fund, and final agreements are still required; financing firms will independently assess demand and viability. NVIDIA’s commitment to cover up to 25% of certain GPU collateral shortfalls adds potential downside if collateral values weaken.
